title: The Modified-Risk Claim and Charitable Rewards
lessons: An age-verified adult smoker receives ZYN marketing using the modified-risk claim FDA authorized for twenty classic ZYN products in June 2026.
The player opens the ZYN Rewards store and finds charitable donations listed beside merchandise and gift cards.

text: Age-verified, adult, a smoker. An email arrives at your desk. It uses a claim the FDA authorized for twenty ZYN products in June 2026. Counsel insists on reading it exactly.

entry-first-1.speaker: COUNSEL
text: I am required to read the claim as authorized: "Using ZYN instead of cigarettes puts you at a lower risk of mouth cancer, heart disease, lung cancer, stroke, emphysema, and chronic bronchitis."

entry-first-2.speaker: PLAYER
text: You listed six diseases before hello.

entry-first-3.speaker: COUNSEL
text: Hello.

entry-first-4.speaker: PLAYER
text: Is this the part where you say FDA approved?

entry-first-5.speaker: COUNSEL
text: No. FDA authorized those products to be marketed with that claim. The agency is careful to say authorized is not approved, and that no tobacco product is safe. I am careful because they are.

choice-first.speaker: COUNSEL
text: You have read the email twice. Your position?

choices.text: If someone already smokes, that's useful information.
"Instead of cigarettes" is doing a lot of work in that sentence.
I don't want a nicotine brand using disease risk as a sales message.

first-1.speaker: COUNSEL
text: The record will reflect that relative-risk information is material to you. For completeness, FDA says quitting entirely does more than any switch. I am obligated to say that. I would say it anyway.

first-2.speaker: COUNSEL
text: Correct. The authorized comparison is ZYN instead of cigarettes. Not ZYN in general. Not ZYN as well as. Instead of.

first-2-1.speaker: PLAYER
text: You looked happy saying "correct."

first-2-2.speaker: COUNSEL
text: Objection. Speculation.

first-3.speaker: COUNSEL
text: Authorization permits the claim. It does not require you to like seeing it in your inbox. Those are separate questions and I only argue the first one.
You open the ZYN Rewards store. Between an Amazon gift card and a metal can, there is a line: Donate to Hope For The Warriors.

entry-return-1.speaker: PLAYER
text: Why is "Donate to Hope For The Warriors" in the same store as an Amazon gift card and a metal can?

entry-return-2.speaker: COUNSEL
text: We Care by ZYN. Members can send points to the listed charities. The brand values a donated point at four cents. I did not choose the number.

entry-return-3.speaker: PLAYER
text: So my nicotine loyalty points become philanthropy.

entry-return-4.speaker: COUNSEL
text: In the amounts, and to the organizations, the program allows. Yes.

entry-return-5.speaker: PLAYER
text: And ZYN itself?

entry-return-6.speaker: COUNSEL
text: The company says it puts three million dollars a year into the program. The featured organizations currently serve veterans, active-duty service members, and their families.

choice-return.speaker: COUNSEL
text: Your cursor is between the hoodie and the donation. I am not going to move it for you.

choices.text: If the points already exist, I'd rather donate them than get another branded thing.
This is still cause marketing attached to a nicotine loyalty program.
I don't want charity used to make the purchase feel better.

return-1.speaker: COUNSEL
text: Your points may be allocated accordingly. No branded hoodie is required.

return-2.speaker: COUNSEL
text: It is both. The charity is real and the brand benefits from it. Neither cancels the other. I have looked for the clause that would, and it does not exist.

return-3.speaker: COUNSEL
text: You are not required to convert a commercial relationship into a moral one.

return-3-1.speaker: PLAYER
text: That was almost human.

return-3-2.speaker: COUNSEL
text: Please strike "almost" from the record.
